learning_outcomes.text: Understand the psychological foundations of user interface design.
Be familiar with methods of user-centered design processes.
Have an overview of common UI concepts.
Have learned and applied evaluation techniques.
Have gained experience in prototyping novel interfaces (e.g., through 3D printing).

syllabus_topics: Theoretical foundations from psychology and interaction design as a basis for user interface design
Overview of different types of traditional user interfaces (e.g., command-line interfaces, graphical user interfaces)
Overview of advanced user interfaces (e.g., mobile interfaces, pen-based interfaces, tangible user interfaces)
Post-real interfaces (e.g., augmented and virtual reality)
Introduction to user studies: quantitative evaluation methods including basics of statistical analysis; qualitative evaluation methods
Interface prototyping with modern technologies (e.g., 3D printing, laser cutting)
teaching_methods: Practical exercise including the development of an interface prototype and evaluation
assessment_rules: To receive credits, students must pass the written exam. Bonus points can be earned for successful participation in the exercises.
